Static structural review of the frozen bytes (hashes: scoring.toml 95f70d6e..., gates/render/judge.toml 930ee183..., gates/constraints/judge.toml 4db26afa..., scored/functional/judge.toml 0a864ac1..., scored/polish/judge.toml 9f184e6a..., scored/visual/judge.toml b4d4f206..., test.sh bd682592..., tools/score.py 13de2b38..., tools/restart_mcp.py 03c1426f...).

(1) scoring.toml lines 1-11: [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2 (sum 1.0, parsed with tomllib); [floors] functional = 0.05. Byte-identical to the template scoring.toml (diff empty). Every listed name has its directory: tests/gates/render, tests/gates/constraints, tests/scored/functional, tests/scored/polish, tests/scored/visual; no extra suite dirs.

(2) All five judge.toml parse with tomllib. [judge] keys are exactly {judge, mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template, mcp_servers}: judge = "claude-code", mode = "batched", isolated = false, prompt_template = "prompt.md"; no model / reasoning_effort / temperature / weight. The header of each file up to the first [[criterion]] is byte-identical to the corresponding template file (diff empty), i.e. timeouts 600/600/9000/900/900 are template-controlled. Only top-level tables are judge, scoring, criterion.

(3) MCP: every file declares name = "playwright", transport = "stdio", command = "playwright-mcp", args = ["--headless", "--isolated", "--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium", "--no-sandbox"]. Only scored/functional/judge.toml:14-18 also declares name = "verifier", command = "/usr/local/bin/python3", args = ["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py", "$APP_RESTART_HELPER"]. test.sh:193 `export APP_RESTART_HELPER="$LOG_DIR/app-restart.sh"` precedes run_suite (test.sh:203-227); helper generated by heredoc + sed placeholders + chmod 755 (test.sh:127-191) and the .used marker is cleared (test.sh:192). The RewardKit 0.1.7 source copy expands env vars in MCP args (agents.py:66 `os.path.expandvars(arg)`). restart_mcp.py exposes the single-use restart_app tool with 55 s timeout and sanitized PATH. The functional prompt uses restart_app only in protocol D (prompt.md:1, :51) and criterion hro_restart (functional judge.toml ~402-407); no other prompt or criterion mentions restart. test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile and .dockerignore are byte-identical to the template.

(4) Criteria: [scoring] aggregation = "all_pass" in both gates, "weighted_mean" in the three scored dims. Counts: render 1, constraints 1, functional 43, polish 5, visual 5 (55 total, ids unique within and across files; name equals id). Gates: both single criteria type = "binary". Functional 43/43 binary, polish 5/5 binary, visual 5/5 likert with points = 5 and five described anchors each. All weights positive (functional total 58.5, polish 12.0, visual 6.0, gates 1.0); all descriptions non-empty. Polish uses integer weights (3, 2) where the template uses 1.0; RewardKit runner.py:151 passes c.get("weight", 1.0) through to arithmetic, so integers are harmless.

(5) Prompts resolve: every prompt_template file exists beside its judge.toml and contains both {app_context} and {criteria} exactly once and no other brace token (grep for [{}]). RewardKit substitutes {criteria} with str.replace (judges.py:133) and runner.py:136-145 requires the placeholder; test.sh:195-201 replaces {app_context} from tests/app_context.md in every tests/*/*/prompt.md. Every hro_* id cross-referenced inside criteria or prompts (e.g. hro_bulk_move, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked) resolves to a real criterion (0 unresolved).

(6) Score plumbing: test.sh runs gates (budget 1500) -> score.py (exit 0 continue / 1 keep detailed zero / else plain zero) -> scored (budget 11100) -> score.py. score.py reads keys render/constraints/functional/polish/visual from each suite reward.json, which RewardKit emits per directory name. Nesting arithmetic with --max-concurrent-agent 1: gates 600+600 = 1200 < 1500; scored 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100; 1500+11100 = 12600 < task.toml [verifier] timeout_sec 13200.

Adversarial attempts: (a) Broken app passing via wiring: a static shell cannot pass because gates are all_pass binary and score.py requires each gate > 0.0 and functional > 0.05 floor; no criterion is likert in a gate; no scored dimension carries a weight in judge.toml that could override scoring.toml. (b) Conforming app failing via wiring: a missing/unexported helper would zero only hro_restart, and here the export, the literal $APP_RESTART_HELPER and the expandvars path agree; prompts contain no stray braces that would break substitution. I found no structural defect. A conforming app could still lose functional credit to a 9000 s batched timeout (judges.py _timeout_scores), but that is workload (row 11), template-controlled, not wiring.
